messages.content:
The `PosixParser` class in the Apache Commons CLI library has a method `parse` with the following signature:

```java
public CommandLine parse(Options options, String[] arguments, boolean stopAtNonOption) throws ParseException
```

The `testStop3` test is calling this `parse` method with the `stopAtNonOption` parameter set to `true`. The purpose of this parameter is to indicate whether parsing should stop once a non-option is encountered in the arguments.

Based on the current bug report, it seems that the `PosixParser` keeps processing tokens after a non-unrecognized long option when `stopAtNonOption` is enabled. This leads to unexpected behavior where tokens after the unrecognized long option are split or burst incorrectly.

Looking at the implementation of the `parse` method in the `PosixParser` class, it iterates over the tokens in the provided arguments and processes each token based on whether it is a double-dash, single dash, option, or argument. If `stopAtNonOption` is enabled and the parser encounters a non-option token that is not recognized, it still adds this token to the parsed command line instead of stopping further processing.

To address this issue, the logic for handling non-option tokens when `stopAtNonOption` is enabled needs to be adjusted to stop further processing and keep the unrecognized tokens as is instead of splitting or bursting them.

The issue likely lies in the processing logic for non-option tokens in the `parse` method of `PosixParser` when `stopAtNonOption` is set to `true`.

Next, I will suggest the method to be fixed.
The issue can be resolved by modifying the `parse` method in the `org.apache.commons.cli.Parser` class.

The method that needs to be fixed is:
```
org.apache.commons.cli.Parser.parse(org.apache.commons.cli.Options, java.lang.String[], boolean)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
